sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 05.03.2022 at about 4.00 pm., when the petitioner was proceeding in his motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-55-V-1899 from Mysore main road by careful manner and when the petitioner was reached (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.5115/2022 Hanumantha Nagar U Turn, BM Road, Bidadi Hobali, Ramanagar taluk, Ramanagar District, at that time, Lorry bearing reg.No.TN-39-BB-0299 came and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Bidadi Bharath Kempanna Hospital and after first aid treatment, he admitted to Smt.Jayadevi Memorial Hospital, Chikkagollarahatti, Magadi main road, Bangalore - 560 091 wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for 40 days and spent more than Rs.10 lakhs towards medical expenses.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was doing electrician work and earning monthly Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to said accident, he lost his future income.
The Bidadi police have registered a criminal case in crime No.0098/2022 under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.5115/2022 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

3. After service of summons, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court remained absent hence, placed exparte and respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal and filed its written statement.
4. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable in law or on facts of the same.
It has admitted the issuance of the policy in favour of the respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2 has denied the involvement of the Lorry bearing No.TN-39-BB-0299 in the alleged accident.
It has denied the age, occupation, income and amount spent by the petitioner.

Further contended that, the owner of the vehicle did not report and furnished the RTO documents pertaining to the Goods Carrier regarding the driving licence of the person who was driving the vehicle at the time of accident which required under (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.5115/2022 Section 134(C) and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.158(6) of MV Act.
It has contented that, at the time of accident, the driver of the Lorry does not posses valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.

Further contended that,
the alleged accident occurred only due to the negligence of petitioner himself as he was riding the same without wearing helmet and DL at a high speed.

Further contended that, the claim petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper parties as the petitioner not impleaded the owner and the insurer of motor cycle bearing No.KA-55-V-1899 even though they are necessary and proper Jeevan Gowda M.S vs Mani M on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35062089/
2 parties for adjudication of the claim petition.

sentences.text: With these grounds the respondent No.2 sought for rejecting the claim petition.
5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner prove that, he has (SCCH-9) 6 MVC.No.5115/2022 sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 05.03.2022 at about 4.00 pm., on Hanumanthanagar U Turn, B.M.Road, Bidadi Hobali, Ramanagar Taluk,
Ramanagar, due to rash and negligent act of driving of the Lorry bearing reg.No.TN-39-BB-0299 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
6.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1.
Dr.Shailesh A.V has examined as PW.2 and in all got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P.19.
On the other hand, A.O. has examined as RW.1 and got marked 3 documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3 and closed their side evidence.

7. Heard arguments and perused the materials available on record.
8.

The learned counsel for petitioner has relied upon the following citations:

 - MFA No.5468/2010 (MV)

9.
My answer to the above issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:

10. Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioner that, on 05.03.2022 at about 4.00 pm., when he was proceeding in his motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-55-V-1899 from Mysore main road by careful Jeevan Gowda M.S vs Mani M on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35062089/

sentences.text: Due to said impact, he sustained (SCCH-9) 8 MVC.No.5115/2022 grievous injuries.
11. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself examined as PW1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief-examination and reiterated all the facts mentioned in the petition.

He also got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P.15 which are FIR, complaint, spot panchanama, wound certificate, notice, reply to notice,
chargesheet, discharge summaries, medical bills and prescriptions and Aadhar card.
12. On perusal of police documents which are marked at Ex-P1 to Ex-P8 it is clear that the accident took place on 05.03.2022 at about 4.00 pm., and Ex
FIR in crime No.0098/2022 came to be registered on the same day of accident at 20.00 i.e., at Bidadi Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.2 - complaint lodged by relative of petitioner by name Yeshwanth.C.S. on 05.03.2022.
Ex.P.3 is the spot panchanama which describe the spot of accident at Bengaluru-Mysore.
Ex.P.5 is the notice given to the owner (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.5115/2022 of the offending Lorry herein and Ex.P.6 is the reply to the said notice.

Ex.P.7 is the IMV report which shows the front right side bumper damages found to the vehicle bearing No.TN-39-BB-0299 (HGV)
due to impact and front wheel & mudguard, front suspension, head light and indicator assembly,
handle bar, crash guard, speedo meter, fuel tank, front right side foot rest, silencer and rear right side body damages found to the vehicle bearing No.KA-55-V- 1899.

Ex.P.8 is the charge sheet which has been filed against petitioner for the offences punishable under Section 3(1), 4 r/w.S.181 of MV Act and under Section 279 of IPC and of the offences punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC against driver of the offending Lorry bearing reg.No.TN-39-BB-0299.
13.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1.

In his cross-examination he has deposed that, he was born on 16.05.2003 and admitted (SCCH-9) 10 MVC.No.5115/2022 that, charge sheet is filed against him as at the time of accident he was not holding driving licence.
Further PW.1 denied the suggestions made by the learned counsel for the respondent regarding sole negligence of petitioner.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.

There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive and on perusal of the same charge sheet is also filed against the petitioner himself as he was not holding driving licence and filed under Section 5(1) r/w 180 IMV Act.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the contributory negligence of petitioner who was riding the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-55-V-1899 and also by the driver of the offending Lorry bearing reg.No.TN-39-BB-0299 which belongs to the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is its insurer.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 partly in the (SCCH-9) 11 MVC.No.5115/2022 Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:
In view of answering Issue No.1 partly in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries,
pain and suffering, sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc. let me discuss one by one:

4 a) Towards Injury, Pain and Suffering:

sentences.text: The petitioner has contended due to accident he was sustained grievous injuries fracture of right maxilla with fracture of anterior and posterior wall of frontal sinus with SDH right frontal convexity with pneumo - Crphalus and all over the body with abrasion.

In order to prove injuries caused to him, he has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P.4 issued by Bharath Kempanna Multispeciality Hospital (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.5115/2022 which reveals that petitioner has sustained fracture anterior and posterior walls of right frontal sinus, right tentorial bleed is seen, mild frontal and maxillary hemosinus, fracture of right frontal bone and left peri orbital soft tissue swelling and traumacti brain injury and doctor has opined that injury is grievous in nature.

Further, Petitioner examined Dr.Shailesh as PW.2 and through him got marked OPD record, X-ray report, neuro psychological assessment report and mini mental state examination report in all got marked at Ex.P.16 to Ex.P.19.
PW.2 has assessed the disability of petitioner.
Therefore, by considering the injury and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.

b) Towards Medical Expenses: Petitioner has produced 60 medical bills for a sum of Rs.6,26,818/-
which are marked at Ex.P.12, 15 advance receipt marked (SCCH-9) 13 MVC.No.5115/2022 at Ex.P.13 and 22 prescription marked at Ex.P.14.
During cross examination of Pw.1, Respondent No.2 has not put any suggestion therefore, it has been considered that, those medical bills are genuine and correct.
Therefore it is just and reasonable to award Rs.6,26,818/- under the head medical expenses.

c) Towards food, extra nourishment, Conveyance and medical attendant charges: PW.1 has deposed that, immediately after accident he took treatment at Bharath Kempanna Hospital, Bidadi after first aid treatment finally as per discharge summary marked at Ex.P.9, he admitted at Smt.Jayadevi Memorial Hospital, Chikkagollarahatti, Magadi main road, Bengaluru from 06.03.2022 to 13.03.2022 for 8 days, as per Ex.P.10 again from 17.03.2022 to 25.03.2022 for 9 days and as per Ex.P.11 again from 29.04.2022 to 20.05.2022 for 22 days, in total for 39 days petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at Smt.Jayadevi Memorial (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.5115/2022 Hospital.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 39 days and by including conveyance, in all a sum of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment, conveyance and medical attendant charges.
d) Towards Loss of Income during treatment:
The petitioner contended that he was doing Electrician work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Petitioner has not produced to prove his income.

So in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to this Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.
Accordingly, the fixed notional income of the year 2022 at 15,500/- p.m., Petitioner may took 3 months rest and he may lost income for those rest periods.

Therefore, by considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is entitled to Rs.46,500/-

5 (SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.5115/2022 (Rs.15,500/- x 3) towards loss of income during treatment period.

sentences.text: e) Towards Future Earnings:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident he took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital and has become permanently disabled.
The petitioner has examined Dr.Shailesh, Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bangalore as PW.2.

He has contended that, Petitioner sustained injury to head and had seizures, initially he has been treated at NIMHANS,
subsequently he was admitted and treated at Smt.Jayadevi Hospital, he had fracture right frontal subdural hematoma, pneumocephalus, right maxilla, fracture frontal sinus.
Further contended that, he has impaired memory and intelligence, skull X-ray done which revealed evidence of right frontal craniotomy, bone flap seen in situ.
Pychological assessment was done on 13.04.2024 and his IQ was 82.
PW.2 further contended that, petitioner is having below average in thinking and (SCCH-9) 16 MVC.No.5115/2022 reasoning, his parietal lobes were slow in functioning.
On IDEAS, he obtained a score of 07, suggestive of 40-70% disability.
MMSE was done and petitioner obtained a low score of 23/30.

Further PW.2 contended that,
petitioner her borderline intellectual disability around 10% and it is pertaining to the whole body likely to be permanent.
During cross examination PW.2 has deposed that,    .

It is relevant to note that PW.2 has assessed disability to the whole body at 10%.

It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the (SCCH-9) 17 MVC.No.5115/2022 particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

By looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side as the petitioner himself has given his evidence and he himself has put his signature on his evidence.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 8% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P.15 - Aadhar card in order to prove his age.
As per said document, he was born on 16.05.2003 and as on date of accident he was aged about 19 years.

Under such circumstances, the age of petitioner was considered as 19 years and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and the proper multiplier is "18" is applicable as per Smt.Sarala Verma's case.

Hence future earning capacity of the petitioner due (SCCH-9) 18 MVC.No.5115/2022 to Jeevan Gowda M.S vs Mani M on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35062089/
6 permanent disability works out as under:
15,500 x 12 x 18 x 8% = Rs.2,67,840/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled Rs.2,67,840/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.

The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he cannot carryout his work/any manual work.

Regarding Liability:

The respondent No.2 has taken contention that, the petitioner is sole Jeevan Gowda M.S vs Mani M on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35062089/
7 negligence to the alleged accident and he himself is liable to the occurrence of accident.

sentences.text: Further it is the contention of the respondent No.2 that, driver of the offending vehicle not (SCCH-9) 20 MVC.No.5115/2022 holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

Further the respondent No.2 has taken another defense that, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed for non joinder of necessary party i.e., owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-55-V-1899.

Respondent No.2 has examined its A.O. as RW.1 who has contended that, as on the date of accident the petitioner being a minor himself was riding the motor cycle along with pillion rider and the jurisdictional investigation officer after investigation has filed chargesheet against the juvenile accused for riding motor cycle/petitioner himself and also against the owner of the motor cycle for entrusting the motor cycle to an under aged person under Section 279, 338 of IPC and Section 180,
5(1), 181, 3(1), 4 of MV Act.
The petitioner has relied upon citation cited supra wherein it is noted that, even though the claimant was (SCCH-9) 21 MVC.No.5115/2022 minor he cannot be attributed 50% of contributory negligence only on the ground that claimant was minor.
But wherein case on hand, the charge sheet is itself filed against the petitioner under Section 5(1) r/w 180, 3(1), 4 r/ w 181,MV Act.
Wherein it discloses that, there is contributory negligence in occurrence of alleged accident by the petitioner also.
Moreover, Respondent No.2 has not made effort to prove that, accident occurred only due to sole negligence of the petitioner and not by the driver of the offending lorry.
If it really true, respondent had to prove the same with documentary evidence, but respondent not made any effort to produce the document to prove his defense towards the negligence of lorry driver.
Thus, it is already held that accident was occurred also due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Lorry bearing reg.No.TN-39-BB- 0299 along with petitioner himself.
Therefore, contributory negligence can be attributed 50% each towards petitioner (SCCH-9) 22 MVC.No.5115/2022 as well as the driver of the offending Lorry herein.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C.Owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Lorry bearing reg.No.TN-39-BB-0299 are jointly and severally liable to pay only 50% compensation to the petitioner.

However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay 50% compensation amount among .10,51,158/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is only entitled 50% of total (SCCH-9) 23 MVC.No.5115/2022 compensation amount of .10,51,158/- (Rupees ten lakhs fifty one thousnd one hundred and fifty eight only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive and on perusal of the same charge sheet is also filed against the petitioner himself as he was not holding driving licence and filed under Section 5(1) r/w 180 IMV Act.
PW.2 has assessed the disability of petitioner.
Therefore, by considering the injury and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
The petitioner contended that he was doing Electrician work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
So in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to this Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.
Therefore, by considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is entitled to Rs.46,500/-
